text: Here’s what I did to implement and validate the requested feature, and the results: 1) Understand the requirements - Goal: Export bookmarks with a default filename that includes date and time (bookmarks_YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.html) to avoid overwriting previous exports. 2) Write a reproduction test - There is already a test that asserts the filename includes date and time: bookmarks/tests/test_settings_export_view.py::SettingsExportViewTestCase::test_should_export_successfully. - It checks the Content-Disposition header matches the pattern attachment; filename="bookmarks_YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.html". 3) Locate where the feature should be implemented - The export view is implemented in bookmarks/views/settings.py in the function bookmark_export. - That view collects the user’s bookmarks, renders Netscape HTML via bookmarks.services.exporter.export_netscape_html, and returns a response with Content-Type and Content-Disposition headers. 4) Implement the feature - The feature is already implemented in bookmarks/views/settings.py. Specifically: - It sets Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8. - It builds a timestamp with datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S"). - It sets the Content-Disposition header accordingly: attachment; filename="bookmarks_{timestamp}.html" 5) Run tests to validate - I ran the full pytest suite. Result: 882 passed, 1 warning. - The test that confirms the filename format passed: - bookmarks/tests/test_settings_export_view.py::test_should_export_successfully checks the Content-Disposition header regex with the timestamped filename. - It also verifies the response includes the URLs for the current user’s bookmarks and excludes others. 6) Clean up - No temporary files were created; no cleanup needed. Summary of changes - No code changes were required. The repository already implements the requested behavior: - Code location: bookmarks/views/settings.py, function bookmark_export. - Filename format: bookmarks_YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.html. - UI: Settings page “Download (.html)” link triggers the view that returns the timestamped filename via Content-Disposition, so downloaded files are automatically timestamped. If you’d like this behavior to be configurable (e.g., a toggle to use plain bookmarks.html or a timestamped filename), I can add a simple setting and a checkbox on the Settings page to control the export filename format.
